samb-p01.speaker: Utpaladeva (siddha voice), with the Buddhist opponent staged in his own voice (p. 4)
samb-p01.question: Does 'sambandha' name anything real, or is relation merely thought (kalpanā)?
premises: Benediction (v. 1): to him whose self is relation as unity-in-diversity, accomplisher of all objects, whose work is world-transaction — him, Śiva, of his own will, we praise (svecchayā = seed of svātantrya).
Opening (v. 2): victory to the one light, world-self, whose body dawns as relation through being-and-difference.
The synonyms (saṃsarga/saṃparka/saṃśleṣa/saṃbandha) explain nothing: sense does not rise from parts; like tailapāyika, mere convention (saṃketamātra).
nairantarya fails: distant father/son would have none; adjacent iron bars would count. Neither necessary nor sufficient.
dviṣṭhatā fails: duality and separateness would be relations; 'residing-in-two' is said of the related pair, not the relation. State it in its own form (svarūpeṇaiva spaṣṭam ucyatām).
apekṣā/pāratantrya need consciousness: inert things cannot await; will is consciousness's; what lacks a self cannot await. Dependence-language smuggles in the conscious relatum the Buddhist denies.
Positive thesis: fusion = unity of the many (anekasya ekatā), neither manyness nor unity alone, but what requires both states. One relation per pair (pratiyugalam evaikaḥ saṃbandhaḥ).

Inventory: father-son, king-man, tree-branch, blue-lotus, Devadatta cooking rice, absence of pot, this-other-than-that — and reversed. Framing question: mere seeming or does the real show itself thus?

Buddhist position (p. 4): things complete in themselves, cut off; perception shines the self; thought is fabrication (kalpanā kalpitā eva sā). Proof-text: saṃyujyante na bhidyante svato 'rthāḥ pāramārthikāḥ. Unity-in-multiplicity = contradiction. 'King's man' = usage for worldly business, admitted only at seeming-time, a bhrama persisting like snake-rope, dignified as saṃvṛti.

Retorsion (pp. 5–6): you yourselves admitted the seeming-of-many-as-one (tatrocyate pratītis tāvat...bhavadbhir apy abhyupagataiva). kalpanārūpatvaṃ ca nāsyā doṣaḥ — thought-formedness is no flaw. Thought is not other than the thing's shining (na ca vikalpo 'rthapratibhāsād bhinnaḥ, refutation of thoughtlessness, ĪPK). Admit the shining itself as many-as-one-manifestation. It holds: the ultimately real thing is consciousness-only, world-selved through Māyā-śakti.

Consequences (pp. 6–7): one relation in form, many in coloring. Relation-talk belongs to the Māyā-state. Helper/helped must be stated or transaction ceases (vyavahāralopaḥ). Helping is the consciousness-Lord's will (cinmayeśvarecchāiva sā): two successive things shone together in one reflection (ekaparāmarśāt). Iti na kācit khaṇḍanā.
samb-p01.inference: Every reduction of relation fails (nairantarya, dviṣṭhatā, apekṣā/pāratantrya); the Buddhist's own position presupposes what it denies (retorsion); relation is a real subtle power (śakti) whose form is unity-in-diversity (bhedābheda), grounded in vimarśa. The engine is identity of the action with its self-consciousness: relation is not a category added to content but the reflexive grasping that makes content determinate at all. Dharmakīrti's nominalism makes the general form of relation an inference; Utpala shows it is the condition of inference. (Berger 2024; MacCracken 2022.)
samb-p01.conclusion: Relation is real, not kalpanā. Its form is unity-in-diversity; its locus is vimarśa; its marks are nirbādha (unsublated) and upayogavān (useful). If relations fall, transaction, scripture, and recognition fall with them.
samb-p01.theorem: sambandha = anekasya ekatā (unity of the many), grounded in vimarśa, not kalpanā.

samb-p02.speaker: Utpaladeva, continuing (siddha voice)
samb-p02.question: Granted that relation is real — how does it work? By what operation does thought bind many into one without falsifying them?
premises: Restraint (v. 10): vyāpāro 'nena ruddho 'sau na vikalpāntaraṃ spṛśet | vikalpāntarasaṃsparśe mātṛbhedaprasaṅgataḥ — by this, activity restrained, it does not touch another thought, for touching another thought would entail knower-difference. Relation holds the manifold from scattering, not gluing alien bits. This restraint is the mode of intentional action (śakti): reflexive grasping keeping content determinate without collapsing into identity or difference.

One-reflection, one-word-superimposition (v. 11): tadekāmarśavarty ekaśabdādhyāsavaśād brajet | aneko 'py ekatām artho yathā ghaṭapaṭāv iti — resting in one-reflection, by superimposing one word, the many go to oneness of meaning, as 'pot and cloth.' The dvandva is the proof: many things, one word, one meaning — because one reflection.

Qualifier for help (vv. 12–13): saṃbandha upakārārthaḥ sa jñātum upayujyate — relation is for the sake of helping; worth knowing. Even in duality there is two-ness of qualifier and qualified: as the king's horses-chariots-soldiers rest on two reflections. One reflection toward the king (facing his own generality); another toward the man (bearing king-generality-relation). Rājñaḥ puruṣaḥ comes after — it is relation-ranged.

Genitive's seat (vv. 14–15): the genitive-voiced relation sits in the qualifier that has attained qualified-oneness, without abandoning its own form. Loss of one reading, purity of the principal, joining of other with other.

Transfer across principals (vv. 16–18): as the king's man may be the brahmin's too, so oneness with another principal — or with a further one — is called the subordinate's relation: as the king's horse, the king's man. Relation rides the subordinate term across principals; the pair, not the substance, carries it.
samb-p02.inference: Relation operates by restraint (holding the manifold), one-reflection (one word, one meaning), qualifier/qualified structure (for help), genitive seat (in the qualifier), and transfer across principals. The engine is reflexive grasping (vimarśa) — not a concept but the mode of intentional action that keeps content determinate. Relation exists in order to help knowing.
samb-p02.conclusion: Relation's machinery: restraint → one-reflection → qualifier-for-help → genitive's seat → transfer. The payoff (upakārārthaḥ): relation exists in order to help knowing.
samb-p02.theorem: Relation = anekasya ekatā via ekāmarśa + viśeṣaṇa/viśeṣya, for upakāra.
unresolved_terms: Kalpyo 'nena — exact force of singular (one superimposed) vs. two; verse compressed, edition punctuation editorial

samb-p03.speaker: Utpaladeva, concluding (siddha voice)
samb-p03.question: If relation is real but belongs to the Māyā-state, are its users deluded?
premises: Established by relation's course (v. 19): iti saṃbandhagatyā uktā māyīyajñātṛniṣṭhitāḥ | dhiyo vibhinnārthadṛśo vyavahārapravartikāḥ — thus, by relation's course, are stated the Māyā-knower-established intellects of diverse-thing-view that drive transaction. Relation's course (gati) is what establishes finite knowers and their business.

Not simply deluded (v. 20a): na paraṃ tās tathā bhrāntāḥ sarvā api pratikṣaṇāt — yet they are not simply deluded, all of them, at every moment. Against the opponent's bhrama/saṃvṛti verdict: error-status is not the whole story.

Grounded in self-awareness (v. 20b): svasaṃvitsaṃjñakānantacidvimarśapratiṣṭhitāḥ — grounded in the infinite consciousness-reflection called self-awareness. Ground of transaction-intellects is not correspondence with cut-off things but rootedness in infinite vimarśa. vimarśa is consciousness not merely reflecting but actively grasping itself (Ratié: 'apprehends or grasps that manifestation actively and spontaneously'). Pratyabhijñā philosophers deliberately appropriate Buddhist concepts, taking full responsibility. The closing pūrṇaḥ parikaraḥ names this: relation, self-awareness-accomplished, is the whole philosophical apparatus the Recognition brings.

The seal (v. 21): uktaḥ svasaṃvitsiddhaḥ … saṃbandhaḥ … nirbādha upayogavān | … pūrṇaḥ parikaraḥ … pratyabhijñāyām — stated: the self-awareness-accomplished relation — unobstructed, useful — the full retinue in the Recognition. nirbādha (no cognition sublates it) + upayogavān (it does work) = the two marks of the real, earned back from the Buddhist's own criteria.
samb-p03.inference: Relation's course establishes finite knowers and transaction; they are not simply deluded because grounded in infinite vimarśa (svasaṃvit); the seal's two marks (nirbādha + upayogavān) earn back the real from the Buddhist's own criteria. Relation is unobstructed and useful — the full retinue (parikaraḥ) of the Recognition.
samb-p03.conclusion: Relation is real. Self-awareness-accomplished, it is unobstructed and useful — the full retinue of the Recognition. The Māyā-knowers' intellects drive transaction and are not simply deluded, because they rest on infinite vimarśa.
samb-p03.theorem: saṃbandha = svasaṃvitsiddhaḥ, nirbādha, upayogavān, pūrṇaḥ parikaraḥ pratyabhijñāyām.
unresolved_terms: pratikṣaṇāt scope — 'not deluded at every moment' leaves open which moments escape delusion; text does not schedule them
parikaraḥ (retinue/entourage) — closing metaphor unexpanded; read as 'the full philosophical apparatus the Recognition brings with it'
